Implement a Python 3.12 function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that accepts an iterable of integer `(start, end)` pairs and returns a new list of disjoint intervals sorted by start. Reject pairs whose start exceeds end with `ValueError`. Merge touching intervals as well as overlapping ones, do not mutate the input, and handle an empty iterable. Include type hints, a concise docstring, and `pytest` tests covering empty input, unsorted input, nested intervals, touching boundaries, negative values, duplicate intervals, and invalid pairs. Explain the time and space complexity after the code.
